recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The End of COVID Summit Explained", "body": "Mike Winner described the End of COVID summit as a free online education that begins July 11th, with over 90 sessions and almost 200 hours of content offered free for 21 days. He said the program is laid out like a film, with acts and modules, and ends with sessions on a new health story. Chance Garton framed its value as retrospective, arguing that seeing the whole pattern lets people spot the next attempt sooner. Amandha Vollmer, Mike Stone and Jacob Diaz each described the sessions they hosted or joined, and Chance closed by asking listeners to share the event."}, {"title": "Scrutinizing Studies and Cell Cultures", "body": "Amandha Vollmer said she opened every study a doctor cited for detoxing spike protein and found only in vitro work, which she called the same cell culture magic show. Jacob Diaz argued that virology grows monkey cells in a soup of antibiotics and serum, then labels the breakdown particles as viruses without ever seeing them in the original sample. Mike Stone claimed the foundational virology papers lack an independent variable and so fail the scientific method, making them pseudoscience by definition. Amandha added that she hopes the summit leaves people able to read a study with a critical eye."}, {"title": "Animal Labs and Cruel Experiments", "body": "Amandha Vollmer recounted working as an assistant at a University of Alberta animal facility, where she said failed experiments meant euthanizing animals and starting again, and where data was cherry picked to win approval for drug trials. She described the whole experience as a waste of life that made her question whether it was science at all. Mike Stone argued that early virology experiments involved drilling into monkeys' heads and injecting tissue, while Jacob Diaz said bacteriology used the same methods, which he called the roots of germ theory. They framed this as a hidden cost of the field."}, {"title": "Mind, Symbolism and Contagion", "body": "Chance Garton recommended Tuning the Human Biofield and Metaphysical Anatomy, arguing that every malady carries a symbolic message and that reading it can undo the pattern behind it. Jacob Diaz argued that energy, not germs, explains what gets labeled contagion, pointing to shared laughter, synced cycles and placebo and nocebo studies where belief produced symptoms. Mike Stone said fear and stress, including nonstop media reports, lockdowns and masking, can produce the same symptoms attributed to COVID. All three treated belief and emotion as central to health."}, {"title": "Mystery, Starlink and the Boötes Kite", "body": "Chance Garton told of a line of light and a green fireball crossing the sky while discussing why mystery matters, arguing that supernatural events always leave room for doubt. He wondered aloud whether such a line could be plasma beings or the seraphim of ancient texts. Gabe argued that a government graphic of a black diamond craft matches the stars of Boötes, whose name means kite, and tied it to the Benjamin Franklin kite story as a kind of spell. Gabe also predicted a philosophical wedge over whether nukes are real."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: They've announced that its over, but what if it never began in the first place? Now that the big show is over, Mike Winner of Alfa Vedic and his all-star team are collaborating to bring us an online summit that retrospectively demonstrates the deceptions of the past few years, so that we can ensure nobody ever falls for it again.
